raw: 37.1 What Is Cognitive Security? Definitions, Scope, Emergence[^165][^166][^167]
teaching_note: Cognitive security concerns conditions that protect informed, autonomous thinking and decision-making against information-related harms; definitions differ over whether the unit is a person, organization, or information environment. Cognitive warfare is a contested strategic/military framing, not a synonym for every cognitive-security problem: an ordinary mistaken notice does not establish an adversarial campaign. Neither term licenses deciding which opinions people may hold or treating biological/psychological/social labels as a universally validated taxonomy. The research article and its LinkedIn announcement are one underlying publication, not independent corroboration [@ageint165; @ageint167]; compare definitional scope rather than counting URLs.
title: What Is Cognitive Security? Definitions, Scope, Emergence

raw: 37.1.1 Comprehensive Definition: State and Process Against Malign Influence[^166]
teaching_note: A state of cognitive security describes a desired condition; a process describes ongoing source checking, correction, and rights-preserving response. Calling an influence malign requires evidence of the relevant conduct and intent, not merely disagreement or an emotional reaction. Treat the cited concept analysis as a definitional proposal, not an instrument that measures individual security or identifies malicious people [@ageint166].
title: Comprehensive Definition: State and Process Against Malign Influence

raw: 37.1.2 Cognitive Security vs. Cybersecurity vs. Information Security[^95]
teaching_note: Information security protects information's confidentiality, integrity, and availability; cybersecurity addresses risks in digital systems; cognitive security asks how information conditions affect judgment and autonomy. A technically intact message can still be misleading, while a mistaken message need not result from a cyber intrusion. Epistemic security additionally concerns institutions and practices through which knowledge is produced, checked, and distributed [@ageint173; @ageint175]; these scopes overlap without being interchangeable.
title: Cognitive Security vs. Cybersecurity vs. Information Security

raw: 37.1.3 Three Pillars: Awareness + Situation Awareness + Purposeful Action[^166]
teaching_note: Use the three-pillar formulation as an attributed organizing model: awareness identifies a possible information problem, situation awareness places it in a specific evidence context, and purposeful action selects a proportionate response. In a synthetic notice exercise, noticing an inconsistent date is awareness; checking the supplied dated original is situation awareness; holding the draft until the date is resolved is action. This sequence does not establish a validated psychological taxonomy or guarantee resistance [@ageint166].
title: Three Pillars: Awareness + Situation Awareness + Purposeful Action

raw: 37.2 Unveiling the Multifaceted Concept of Cognitive Security (Elsevier, 2025)[^165][^167]
teaching_note: A literature review can map competing definitions and research gaps without showing that a single intervention works across them. Compare each definition's protected object, assumed threat, observable outcome, and rights implications; an individual recognition test and an institutional information-quality assessment answer different questions. The announcement is publication context only; it cannot independently validate the review's proposed redefinition [@ageint165; @ageint167].
title: Unveiling the Multifaceted Concept of Cognitive Security (Elsevier, 2025)

raw: 37.3 Cognitive Security in the Age of AI (RESAID Policy Paper, 2025)[^95]
teaching_note: Read the inherited RESAID heading as a policy-paper attribution, not neuroscience evidence. A proposal for public institutions or AI safeguards must specify authority, accountability, dissent protection, and a reviewable harm claim; institutional ambition is not measured effectiveness. The supplied citation is a policy source, and its recommendations do not themselves authorize surveillance, message targeting, or belief monitoring [@ageint095].
title: Cognitive Security in the Age of AI: Policy Perspective

raw: 37.4 AI Development Should Prioritize Cognitive Security (NeurIPS Position Paper, 2023)[^96]
teaching_note: The raw heading preserves inherited venue/year wording; use this source as an AI-policy position paper rather than endorsing that unverified NeurIPS-2023 attribution. Proposing research on AI influence, belief-change metrics, and safeguards is different from demonstrating safe interventions or reliable intent detection. A defensible classroom question is whether a proposed metric distinguishes informed choice from compliance, not how to optimize persuasion of a selected audience [@ageint096].
title: AI Development Should Prioritize Cognitive Security: Position Paper

raw: 37.4.1 DARPA Intrinsic Cognitive Security (ICS) Program[^168][^169][^170]
teaching_note: DARPA ICS is a mixed-reality research program seeking cognitive safeguards and formal methods; aims, solicitation details, and demonstrated results are different evidence classes. News and procurement listings describe the same program, not three independent efficacy studies. Its mixed-reality scope must not be transferred into a claim of general LLM cognitive-security guarantees [@ageint169].
title: DARPA Intrinsic Cognitive Security (ICS) Program

raw: 37.4.2 Mixed Reality Cognitive Attack Typology[^171]
teaching_note: Here typology concerns mixed-reality information hazards, not financial due diligence. A paper-only classroom classification can distinguish an obstructed field of view, conflicting simulated labels, and excessive alerts by their potential effects on perception and attention; it must not induce those effects in a person or device. The Reddit item is discovery/provenance, not a validated attack taxonomy; DARPA's official program description supports the research context only [@ageint171; @ageint169].
title: Mixed-Reality Cognitive Hazard Literacy

raw: 37.4.3 Formal Methods for Cognitive Guarantees in MR Systems[^169]
teaching_note: A formal guarantee has premises: a specified system, environment, model of human interaction, property, and proof assumptions. Proving an alert-rate property in a model does not prove that all users remain attentive, that a clinical symptom cannot occur, or that an LLM is secure. Ask what happens when the cognitive model or sensor assumptions fail; an unmodeled condition leaves the real-world claim unestablished [@ageint169].
title: Model-Scoped Formal Methods for Mixed-Reality Safeguards

raw: 37.5 Behavioral Outcomes of Human Cognitive Security (arXiv, March 2026)[^107]
teaching_note: Distinguish veracity discernment, task-oriented action, and information sharing: recognizing an unsupported claim does not imply withholding it, and sharing can have motives other than belief. The cited framework is a modeling contribution, not validation of a universal human-agent isomorphism or proof of an intervention's effect. Keep observed task responses separate from explanations of the respondent's intent [@ageint107].
title: Behavioral Outcomes of Human Cognitive Security (arXiv, March 2026)

raw: 37.6 Defining Comprehensive Cognitive Security in the Digital Era (SSRN 2024)[^166]
teaching_note: Operationalize a broad definition by specifying what would count as improvement and what would count against it. Faster agreement is not necessarily better informed judgment; a reader who asks for missing evidence may be exercising autonomy rather than showing insecurity. A concept analysis supplies vocabulary and candidate boundaries, not a psychometric scale or a causal intervention evaluation [@ageint166].
title: Defining Comprehensive Cognitive Security in the Digital Era (SSRN 2024)

raw: 37.7 Ethics of Cognitive Security (YorkSpace Dissertation)[^172]
teaching_note: Protecting an information environment can itself threaten autonomy if an institution equates dissent with vulnerability or treats its own preferred account as unquestionable. Contrast a transparent correction with covert belief steering: both may change a message environment, but only the former exposes its reasons and allows contestation in this curriculum. The dissertation supplies ethical argument, not legal authorization or empirical proof that a chosen control works [@ageint172].
title: Ethics of Cognitive Security (YorkSpace Dissertation)

raw: 37.8 Epistemic Security: Protecting Knowledge Production and Distribution
teaching_note: Epistemic security examines whether people and institutions can obtain, evaluate, and correct knowledge, including source diversity, trustworthy processes, and access to contrary evidence [@ageint173; @ageint175]. The inherited ICS/DevSecOps/software-development citations describe governance context, not evidence for this definition. A perfectly signed but outdated announcement illustrates why technical provenance alone cannot establish current truth.
title: Epistemic Security: Protecting Knowledge Production and Distribution

raw: 37.8.1 Seger: Epistemic Security as a Field[^173]
teaching_note: A systems view asks how knowledge moves among originators, editors, institutions, platforms, and readers. Three outlets repeating one release provide reach, not independent confirmation; their common origin remains a single dependency. This field framing supports asking about the environment of informed choice, not ranking citizens by supposed epistemic fitness [@ageint173].
title: Seger: Epistemic Security as a Field

raw: 37.8.2 Epistemic Security 2029: Fortifying the UK's Information Supply Chain[^174]
teaching_note: Information supply chain here means the social production and distribution of information, not a software package/build pipeline. Trace a report from an originating record through editorial summaries and recommendation systems to an audience, noting where context or corrections can be lost. The report is a policy analysis and recommendations document; its future-oriented framing is not a measured forecast of conditions in 2029 [@ageint174].
title: Epistemic Security 2029: The UK's Information Supply Chain

raw: 37.8.3 Tackling Threats to Informed Decision-Making (Turing Institute)[^175]
teaching_note: **Completed synthetic scope case.** At 09:00 card A, a fictional museum's dated notice, says the east entrance closes today; at 09:10 card B repeats it but omits east, and at 09:20 card C copies B. The scope matrix records: content claim = whole museum closed (unsupported); provenance = B and C share one origin; cognitive effect = possible confusion (hypothesis, not measured); rights = no basis to label a reader or author malicious. Decision: hold the whole-site closure claim and retain only the east-entrance statement. A supplied 09:30 correction restores east in B, so the revised brief links the correction and marks C stale; missing author intent remains unknown, and no attribution or targeted response follows. This applies the claim workflow in [@sec:analytic-workflow], not a live influence investigation [@ageint175].
title: Tackling Threats to Informed Decision-Making (Turing Institute)

raw: 37.8.4 Epistemic Governance in Crisis: A Complexity Approach[^1]
teaching_note: Complexity language draws attention to feedback, interdependence, and unintended consequences; it does not make a system forecast certain or a governance intervention self-justifying. In the museum case, amplifying an unsupported closure to correct it could increase its reach, while suppressing discussion could conceal a real access problem. Prefer a narrowly sourced correction with visible uncertainty and a reversible classroom decision; the cited conceptual source is not an efficacy trial [@ageint001].
title: Epistemic Governance in Crisis: A Complexity Approach
